summary: The entire surviving correspondence: Wilde congratulating Rennell Rodd on his Second in Greats in December 1880.
certainty_reasoning: The record documents a friendship or acquaintance with no evidence of attraction or romance; classified platonic, upgradable if contrary evidence comes to light.

sources.quote: Dear Rennell, My best congratulations. Greats is the only fine school at Oxford, the only sphere of thought where one can be, simultaneously, brilliant and unreasonable, speculative and well-informed, creative as well as critical, and write with all the passion of youth about the truths which belong to the august serenity of old age. I wish you had got a First, that my compeers should not all be sluggish and syllogistic Scotchmen; still, a Second is perhaps for a man of culture a sweeter atmosphere than the chilly Caucasus of an atheistical First. Come back very soon. Truly yours
sources.context: Wilde to Rennell Rodd, circa 4 December 1880, Keats House (MS Private) - the only letter to Rodd in the volume, congratulating him on his Second in Greats, announced in The Times on 4 December 1880.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The entire surviving correspondence, and the extent of the affection in it: 'Dear Rennell' and 'Come back very soon'.
sources.provenance: PDF pp. 127-128. The letter runs across the page break and is transcribed whole.

date_label: Oxford friendship from the late 1870s; the correspondence survives only for 1880
